market.audience: Adults who want a lightweight way to begin and resume personal routines, including people looking for ADHD-friendly structure
market.problem: Broad planners can show many tasks at once, while an interruption can make it hard to find where a routine left off.
market.advantage: Next Cue puts one scheduled routine first, guides the user through one visible step at a time, and saves a paused run for later. The first routine is free; Pro adds more routines.
market.competitive_context: Routine apps range from full-day visual planners to timer-led habit trackers. Next Cue focuses on a scheduled personal routine, one current step, and a calm way to return after an interruption, without streak pressure or a countdown timer.

proof_points.claim: The Today screen leads with one scheduled routine and a direct start action.
The run screen keeps the current step, progress, and completion controls visible together.
The paused run keeps the current step available with a clear resume action.
The completion screen confirms the finished routine without a timer or streak count.
The routine library keeps separate morning and evening routines with their own schedules.
The editor offers templates plus editable steps and per-step time estimates.

ready_labels: Paused. Come back whenever you’re ready.
You finished the steps in Morning start

story.throughline: Make a routine easier to begin, follow, and return to when the day interrupts

pitch.benefit: See one scheduled routine and a direct way to begin
pitch.problem: A broad list of tasks can leave the first action unclear.
pitch.advantage: Today leads with the next scheduled routine and a clear start action.
pitch.proof: The literal Today screen shows the next routine, its schedule, and Start routine. This frame uses a seeded Pro state because the sample includes morning and evening routines.

frames.header: Keep the next step in view

pitch.benefit: Follow the current step without scanning the full routine
pitch.problem: A checklist can still leave a person deciding which task to do now.
pitch.advantage: The run screen puts one current step, progress, and step controls together.
pitch.proof: The real run screen shows Get out of bed as the current step, with progress and Done with this step.

frames.header: Pick up again after a pause

pitch.benefit: Return to an unfinished routine at its saved step
pitch.problem: An interruption can break a run and make the next action hard to find again.
pitch.advantage: Next Cue saves the current run so the person can pause and resume later.
pitch.proof: The paused screen shows the preserved current step and Resume. A store test also verifies that progress survives relaunch.

frames.header: Finish a routine at your own pace
frames.story_focus: a routine at your own pace

pitch.benefit: Finish a routine without a countdown or a streak requirement
pitch.problem: Timed routines and streak pressure can make a flexible routine feel like a test.
pitch.advantage: Next Cue tracks completed steps and leaves the user free to return when it fits.
pitch.proof: The completion screen celebrates finishing and invites the user back whenever the routine fits.

pitch.benefit: Keep separate morning and evening routines in one library
pitch.problem: One routine may not fit every part of a day.
pitch.advantage: Next Cue Pro adds more routines while the first routine stays free.
pitch.header_problem: one routine for every part of the day
pitch.proof: The library shows the seeded morning and evening routines. Pro is explicit in the header; the first routine remains free.

frames.header: Build routines your way with Pro

pitch.benefit: Start from a template, change each step, and choose the days it fits
pitch.problem: A fixed routine can be hard to use when the steps or schedule do not fit.
pitch.advantage: Next Cue makes steps and weekly reminders editable for each routine.
pitch.proof: The editor shows routine templates, editable steps, reminder time, and selected weekdays. The Pro requirement for adding another routine is named in the header.
